title: Call and response
hookLine: the preacher calls, the people answer: worship as conversation

cards: The preacher is deep into the sermon now, and she isn't talking alone. She says a line, and from the third pew someone answers, "Well!" She says the next one, and from the back, "Preach!"
An organ chord fills the gap. She slows down, leans on the pulpit, and asks the room, "Can I get a witness?" The room answers, "Amen!"
In the Black church tradition, none of that is an interruption. It's how the sermon gets preached. The preacher calls, the people answer, and worship turns into a conversation.

teach.b: The shape is in the Bible too. In Nehemiah, the people gather in the street before the Water Gate in Jerusalem to hear Ezra read the law.
When he opens the book, he blesses God: "And Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God. And all the people answered, Amen, Amen, with lifting up their hands." A call, and an answer.
Amen is the people's word: yes, so be it, this is true.

teach.h: SAY AMEN AT THY GIVING OF THANKS.
teach.b: Paul takes it for granted when he writes to Corinth, asking how a listener who can't follow the prayer could "say Amen at thy giving of thanks." In his churches, people answered.

teach.h: A WITNESS SAYS: I SAW IT TOO.
teach.b: Now the word in today's line: witness. A witness, in a courtroom or in the Bible, is someone who tells what they saw. Before he leaves, Jesus tells his followers in Acts, "ye shall be witnesses unto me."
So when a preacher asks, "Can I get a witness?" the question underneath is: has anybody else seen this? Is this true in your life too? The amen that comes back isn't applause for the preacher.
It's testimony that the word holds. And the conversation runs both ways. A preacher in this tradition listens to the room.
When the answers come quick, the sermon builds. When the room goes quiet, the preacher may circle back and say it again, slower, until it lands. The people help carry the sermon.
Nobody is just the audience. Every voice in the room has a job, even if the job is one word.

how: In Black church worship, congregations answer the preacher during the sermon with words like amen, well and preach, and the preacher listens and responds to them, so the sermon is shaped by the whole room.

o: a sermon read aloud by members, one verse each
a preacher's lines answered aloud by the congregation
a time for questions to the pastor after a sermon

p: amen, amen, with lifting up their hands

s: in call and response, answering the preacher interrupts the sermon
the answers are part of how the sermon gets preached.
in Nehemiah, the people answer Ezra with amen, amen
"and all the people answered, Amen, Amen, with lifting up their hands."

games.q: the preacher leans on the pulpit and asks, "can I get a witness?" what is she asking for?
o: someone to answer that it's true.
a volunteer to come up front.
games.why: she's asking whether anyone else has seen it. the amen that comes back is testimony, not applause.

practice: Bring to mind a line of scripture you know, or a sentence someone once said to you that turned out to be true. If you agree with it, answer it out loud, as quietly as you like: amen.
Then find another true thing, a kindness you received or a lesson learned the hard way, and answer that one too.

wordCard.voice: Call and response. The preacher calls, the people answer, and the sermon is preached by the whole room.
